newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MINISTER SZABO RESIGNS OVER HEALTH SYSTEM.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MINISTER SZABO RESIGNS OVER HEALTH SYSTEM.

text.p: Hungary's Welfare Minister Gyorgy Szabo said on Tuesday he had resigned over differences with the Finance Ministry over the health care system which would continue to be troubled with a lack of funds in 1997.
"Hungarian health care is in a really difficult situation," Szabo, whose resignation had been accepted by Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Monday, told a news conference.

"Not only a cut in expenditures is necessary, we do have to invest money," he added. "The operational ability of the system could be consolidated with spending 20 to 25 billion forints in the next few years."
Szabo said that he could not reach his target in negotiations with the Finance Ministry about the social security -- health and pension -- system's budget.
He added that the institutions in the system would need 270 billion forints for their operations in 1997, but next year's budget would only provide them with 258.5 billion forints.

"I suppose this would lead to the same problems we had this year. Debt grows, hospitals run out of funds for drugs and there are problems in ambulance services," Szabo told Reuters. "People cannot endure that the system cannot take care of them when they are the most helpless."
Szabo will leave its post on November 30. His predecessor has not been named yet.
Szabo is the ninth minister to resign from Horn's coalition government of Socialists and Free Democrats since it was formed in May 1994. All but one have been appointees of Horn's Socialist Party.
